title: Johnson Brothers personnel and Harold Battiste
summary: Ford calls this the best band he worked with, lists its members and describes Harold Battiste, who joined on baritone and later worked with Sonny and Cher.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Deluxe it was, forty-nine. We'll look it up. Yeah, Mellow Mama, that's the name of it. What was it released as? It was released as Mellow Mama. The Johnson Brothers? The Johnson Brothers. The Johnson Brothers. The Johnson Brothers. That's right, Mellow Mama. I believe it was a, because it took us a year to get the money, and at the time it was forty dollars for a recording session, which was still a lot of money. And forty-nine was plenty of money. And, because I played with that band, and that's the best band I ever worked with till the day I think. It is. I know it. It is. Claes Johnson, his sister Gwen sang, Raymond played piano, Lloyd Lambert played bass, same Lloyd who's up there now with me, with Thomas Jefferson. Lloyd Lambert played bass, Edward Blackwell played drums, who went with Arnett Coleman. And Raymond played piano. And Raymond played piano. And Raymond played piano. And Ray Charles played trumpet. He went with Ray Charles later on. He's in New York now. I believe he wrote a couple of tunes for Ray Charles. And then later on, Harold Batiste, who had specialty records here, was the representative, he came in and he played baritone. He came in and played baritone I'd say about 1950, or 51, because he was going to Dillard then, which was a very good clarinet player. And he came in a band and he played baritone. And he's, right now, in fact he's the one that discovered Sonny and Cher. He discovered Sonny, which led to Cher. But he doesn't get any credit for it. We produced all of us early. Well the last time Cher and Sonny came in, he was conducting for them. It was the year I had the accident, because I was on credit the last time I saw them. Nineteen seventy-seven, there with the Fairmount. Sonny and Cher, he was conducting for Sonny and Cher. He discovered Sonny here.
Yeah, well I think Sonny was working for Specialty at the same time. Yeah.

But he's the one that discovered Sonny. He brought him with Specialty. He produced the first record. He found Sonny here? That's what I read. But I know he discovered, he put them together. He put Sonny, he started, made Sonny's first record. Now how Cher got in there, I don't know, but he produced all of their records until they got on a big scale. And he was conducting for them, whenever they were going. He conducted for them all over.
